title: New arenas, districts and pending deals

rows.public_construction_notes: Preliminary agreement on 104 acres of the former Valley View Mall site, about 10 miles north of downtown, for an arena to open by 2031, when the American Airlines Center lease expires (AP via WTOP, June 1 2026); no public financing deal reported. A D Magazine post read earlier reported that Legends was hired as owner's representative and that the site lies in the Mall Area Redevelopment TIF district; it could not be re-read on Oct. 17 2026 (403). The team began the rezoning process in September 2026 (FOX 4, Sept 9 2026); no public financing request reported as of Oct 22 2026.
Included in HOU row as pending: an expected state grant, no agreement found. Pending: an expected state grant; no agreement found

Included in MEM row. Pending: held until a long-term lease is signed; the Oct. 8, 2026 Sports Authority agenda lists a construction manager agreement and a funding-agreement amendment, and press reports their approval; lease unsigned as of Oct. 22, 2026

rows.arena: New Oklahoma City arena (Continental Coliseum, Paycom Center replacement)
rows.opened: late summer 2028 (target); must open by June 2029 (okc.gov); the license agreement's outside completion deadline is June 30 2030, after which the team may terminate
rows.public_construction_notes: 72-month 1-cent sales tax (voters Dec 2023, 71%; projected $976.3M incl. debt service) + MAPS 4: $89M (okc.gov 2026-10-12); $78M (b, OCPPA audited FY2024 report: "City MAPS 4 | Arena | 78,000,000"; okc.gov 2026-03-26; Bond Buyer 2025-10-16); ~$99M (Bond Buyer 2026-05-19); $70M (earlier okc.gov). Public = $900M arena (okc.gov 2026-03-26) - Thunder $50M (computed). $777.15M Series 2026 Arena Sales Tax Revenue Bonds (June 2026; Moody's rated a proposed $800.6M). Bond Buyer (2026-05-19) also reports a temporary 1% use tax approved in December (year not stated; not verified) and pledged revenue of $1.18B. Outside the arena budget: 2025 GO bonds approved by voters Oct 14 2025 (Prop 5 75.52%, Prop 9 75.95%): $35M downtown garage replacing the Myriad parking facility (b, vision.okc.gov, which lists it without naming the arena; the arena link is from Bond Buyer, c) + $25M Thunder front-office buildout (c, Oklahoma Gazette; city lists the line without an amount). Bond Buyer (2026-05-19): $90M of 2025 GO allocated to arena parking, streets and team offices (alternative).
rows.lease_terms: 25 years from move-in, through at least 2053 (Bond Buyer 2026-04-06); early-exit penalties up to $1B in years 1-5 after move-in, $850M in years 6-10, $750M in 11-15, $500M in 16-20 and $250M in 21-25 and each renewal (b, https://www.okc.gov/files/assets/city/v/1/city-manager/documents/pbcarena-use-license-agreementfinal-6-12-25-1.pdf (Arena Use License Agreement, final June 12 2025: s.21.3.5 and Schedule IV, pdf p.103))

to June 30 2035 (b, 2024 interlocal p.9), with a five-year renewal option (2016 interlocal s.5.4.7); the city must negotiate an extension at least as long as the 2027-32 contract bonds before issuing them

rows.public_construction_notes: Teams call it "the largest fully privately funded project in city history" (Sept 2026 renderings); needs City Council approvals; Gov. Shapiro "reaffirmed the state would provide no funding for any new sports arenas" (AP, June 22 2025); no state money found.

Same money as the POR row pending renovation (not double counted). Pending: State up to $365M (SB 1501, enacted, conditional; bond sale expected spring 2027 per DAS) + County up to $88M + City up to $120M (term sheet approved Aug 12 2026, non-binding) = $573M; plus ongoing money (city up to $275.0M over 20 years, county $13.6M) not counted; Multnomah County approved the Joint Authority Agreement Oct 1 2026, which "does not commit the parties to the funding" (Resolution 2026-060), and Portland City Council authorized it Oct 21 2026 (Ordinance 192244, 8-4), which "does not commit the City to any arena lease terms or funding obligations"; its impact statement says the city and Rip City Management "have not yet agreed on the essential terms of a long-term lease"; the agreement lets any party withdraw if definitive documents are not signed by July 1 2028, its "Outside Date" (s.11.4); SB 1501's other conditions must be met by the end of December 2026 for a spring 2027 bond sale (DAS); NBA approval of the sale complete

Bexar County Prop B (Nov 2025, 52.1%): venue tax (hotel 1.75%->2% + 5% car rental) up to $311M or 25% of the cost, whichever is lower (KSAT). Pending: City up to $489M under a non-binding term sheet (Aug 2025, 7-4): the lesser of 38% of the arena cost or $489M (s.2c), expected to be funded in 2028 and conditional on voter passage of a city bond program for the first phase of transportation and pedestrian infrastructure (Financing Addendum, Attachment III); the city's share of district roads and sidewalks for its 2027 bond is now estimated at $35M, about 20% of $175M of projects with the state transportation department assumed to pay 80%, down from $250M a year earlier (San Antonio Report via TPR, Oct 5 2026; not counted); council declined on Aug 17 2026 (5-6) to put the $489M to voters in Nov 2026; separately, council approved Sept 10 2026 up to $60M of Midtown TIRZ debt to buy the 13-acre arena site (more than $115M with financing; final financing plan to return to council; KSAT, TPR); city staff recommended Oct 14 2026 a $442M 2027 general-obligation bond, for a May 2027 vote, that includes the $35M (San Antonio Current, Oct 15 2026); the mayor's alternative leaves out bond money for arena infrastructure (Express-News, Oct 19 2026), and the city manager said a failed bond would force the city to "reexamine the deal" (Express-News, Sept 30 2026); the Spurs say they will build 1,500 parking spaces in garages on the site and that the state transportation department would pay $80M of road work if the bond passes (News 4 San Antonio, Oct 20 2026; the Express-News reported a request to match $21M of city money); definitive agreements targeted by the end of December 2026 (a city official, TPR June 17 2026; the term sheet sets no deadline), not signed as of Oct 22 2026
$375M of the ~$900M 0.5% SLC sales-tax bonds for the surrounding district (not the arena); PID board majority SEG appointees.

rows.arena: Capital One Arena purchase + renovation (2024 deal)
rows.public_construction_notes: $87.5M purchase + $427.5M renovation; included in WAS row.

method: select p.team, p.arena, p.city, p.opened, p.owner, p.row_type, p.construction_cost_nominal_m, p.construction_cost_label, p.public_construction_nominal_m, p.public_renovation_pending_nominal_m, p.private_construction_nominal_m, p.public_construction_notes, p.lease_terms, p.notes_and_gaps, coalesce((select list(s.source_id order by s.field, s.ord) from arena_sources s where s.row_type = p.row_type and s.team = p.team), []) as sources from ledger p where p.row_type like 'project%' order by p.team
